iso_area.note: The storage-class comparison: ROM-resident weights against HBM-resident weights on the same model, workload, numeric profile and technology view. The rom side's silicon is derived (92,450.0 mm2); the hbm side has neither a node count nor a die area in this repository, so the ratio is null and the pair publishes nothing until WP-G fixes the node count at DS41-P3 and a physical record fixes the die area. Stating the denominator as pending is the point of recording it: an iso-area claim against an HBM cluster of unknown silicon would be arithmetic on an invented number.
iso_area.rule: Iso-area rule, DEEPSEEK_V4_ROM_ARRAY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md sections 3.5 and 17 as inherited by DEEPSEEK_V41_FLASH_ROM_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md section 3.5: area is accelerator die area per node times node count, on both sides, and nothing else enters the denominator. HBM stacks, package, switch silicon and board are reported beside the ratio and never inside it. Two sides are iso-area only when their silicon areas agree within the tolerance; when they do not, rule 2 requires the node count that would agree to be stated as a granularity correction, and the pair is published as the control it is rather than as an iso-area ratio.

policy.technology_claim: Predictive ASAP7 research view only; not foundry signoff, manufacturability, or an N4 claim. No DeepSeek-V4.1 token has been produced by any lane in this repository: this document is the pair identity, and every target lock in it is pending. The rom side is two wafer-scale logical devices in a pipeline with one inter-wafer crossing per token (plan section 3.1), carrying one deployment, one session, one event and transaction namespace and one submission, and registered as TopologyClass.WAFER_LOGICAL_DEVICE with node_class WAFER and node_count 2 -- the geometry configs/hardware/abi3_capability/rom_deepseek_v41_wafer.json declares and compiler/backends/rom/deepseek_v41.py lowers against. It is not one wafer of silicon and may not be reported as one: master plan section 3 forbids relabelling a stage pipeline as one oversized chip, and a result carries the topology_class, node_class and node_count of the target that produced it. Its silicon is 2 x 46,225.0 mm2 = 92,450.0 mm2 from the published wafer-die area, which is also the area the roofline's iso-area GPU comparator is derived against for this model (results/roofline/candidates/deepseek-v41-flash/n5_vs_b200/analytical.json#design_selection.models[model=DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash].recommended, device_count 2). The inter-wafer link stays an assumed 5 us hop with a 1-to-10 us sweep (plan risk 4) and is a reported sensitivity, not a point value. The hbm side is the model-blind conventional HBM/SRAM chip replicated to a node count plan section 3.3 derives and WP-G fixes, with the Engram tables in host memory as DeepSeek serves them. Its node count is null and its die area is unavailable here, so this pair has no area denominator yet and iso_area.status is pending: no ratio may be published from it, iso-area or otherwise, until both are locked. Iso-area rule, DEEPSEEK_V4_ROM_ARRAY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md sections 3.5 and 17 as inherited by DEEPSEEK_V41_FLASH_ROM_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md section 3.5: area is accelerator die area per node times node count, on both sides, and nothing else enters the denominator. HBM stacks, package, switch silicon and board are reported beside the ratio and never inside it. Two sides are iso-area only when their silicon areas agree within the tolerance; when they do not, rule 2 requires the node count that would agree to be stated as a granularity correction, and the pair is published as the control it is rather than as an iso-area ratio.

reporting.ratio_publication_rule: Gate DS41-CMP11: every published ratio appears beside its binding constraint and its resident-session count, per role, in the executed comparison artifact that publishes it. A ratio whose two companions are not printed with it is not published. The companions are read from the executed artifact; the analytical antecedent named here is the roofline row the same quantity has at L0 and may be quoted only in a column labelled analytical -- master plan section 11.1 forbids reading it as an executed result, and plan section 1 forbids reading any of it as a TPOT. tools/build_comparison_report.py does not yet read a contract and emits neither companion field, and no V4.1 execution record exists, so this contract publishes no ratio today: iso_area.status and every target lock say so. This pair's iso_area.status is pending, so it publishes no ratio at all; the companions are declared here so the requirement is in force the moment a ratio becomes possible.

node_count_derivation.rule: The smallest node count at which the HBM-resident weight bytes plus the live per-session KV of the admitted concurrency fit in node-local HBM, with the Engram tables in host memory. A capacity FLOOR of 3 nodes and a smallest admissible CLUSTER_N of 8 already exist; the fitted count does not, because it needs the physical plan and therefore the Kernel IR this contract's model binding is still waiting on. The count is a property of the compiled deployment, not of this contract: WP-G derives it and DS41-P3 locks it. It is null here rather than set to the floor because a floor is not a fit, and whichever number lands becomes the denominator of every per-node figure this pair publishes.

silicon.die_area_source: no artifact in this repository states the die area of the shared conventional HBM/SRAM accelerator chip. results/abi3/comparison_deepseek_rom_array_vs_hbm.json#silicon records the same absence for the V4 pair: "hbm declares no geometry, so its die area is a physical grade this comparison may not assume". DS41-PHY10 and the HBM lane's own physical records are what can fill it.

inputs: compiler/backends/rom/deepseek_v41.py module docstring: the V4 one-wafer product does not hold this model (307.5 GB of weights against a 192 GiB wafer ROM), so the primary target is two wafer-scale logical devices carrying one deployment, one session, one event and transaction namespace and one submission
results/iso-node/leading_node_market/analytical.json: wafer_stages 2 for this model on the central N4-class envelope
node_count_derivation.rule: Two, recorded rather than assumed because it is the one geometry four independent artifacts agree on. The class is WAFER_LOGICAL_DEVICE and not CLUSTER_N: runtime/abi3/capability.py validates a class-2 record by feature bit 9 and its fabric rules admit node_class WAFER at two or more nodes (requiring bits 8 and 9 together), and the pair is one submission to one logical accelerator, which is what ADR-003 section 3.3's wafer contract requires. AM-R1's CLUSTER_N names a fabric between separately submitted devices, which this is not.
